description:
You are born into a family that walks for a living: the pochteca, the hereditary merchant-traders of the Aztec empire, who slip out of Tenochtitlan under cover of darkness, dressed as plainly as any farmer so no one can guess how much wealth travels with them. This is what it actually felt like to grow up learning to carry a bundle before you could read the stars, to trade cacao beans and quetzal feathers on roads where a single wrong word could end badly, and to come home, always, at night.

Told gently in the second person, from a boy's first practice bundle to an old man's last quiet walk home across the causeway, this is a calm, sensory journey through daily life in one of history's great trading cities, perfect for winding down and drifting off to sleep.
era_setting: Tenochtitlan and the trade roads of the Aztec empire, roughly the fourteen hundreds to early fifteen hundreds: a canal-laced island capital of canoes, causeways and floating gardens, plain undyed maguey cloaks against nobles' dyed cotton and quetzal feathers, palette of lake blue-grey, adobe ochre, jade green and cacao brown.

An older Mexica trader, broad-shouldered and weathered, greying black hair cut short, a stern but warm face, wearing a plain knee-length maguey cloak like any humble farmer, often carrying a dark wooden walking cane.
A Mexica woman in early middle age, dark hair in a simple braided wrap, a gentle round face, wearing a plain woven skirt and huipil in undyed cotton and earth tones, no jewelry.
A Mexica woman with warm dark eyes, black hair braided and coiled with plain red woven ties, wearing a modest cream and rust-striped huipil and skirt, a small string of plain beads at her neck.
A Mexica boy of about ten years old, thin but sturdy, short black hair, an eager serious face, wearing a small plain maguey-fiber cloak like his father's, bare feet.

shorts.description: He was never a warrior, only a trader who walked farther than most nobles ever would. #aztec #history #shorts

scenes.narration: Your father tests the knots twice before your very first journey as an Aztec trader begins.
You leave the city in darkness, hiding every trace of gold beneath a farmer's plain cloak.
Starlight lies flat on the causeway as your home disappears behind you into black water.
Deep in hill country, robbers are the real danger, and traders stop saying the city's name aloud.
An old trader teaches you the rule for danger: offer the first gift, and never look afraid.
That night you lie awake, understanding why a merchant who dies on the road gets a warrior's funeral.
When the temple fires rise over the water again, something in your chest finally loosens.

shorts.title: The Aztec Merchant Who Was Also a Spy #shorts
shorts.description: Traders of the Aztec empire carried more than goods, they carried secrets. #aztec #history #shorts

scenes.narration: Slowly you notice things nobody taught you: how many warriors guard a gate, how nervous a chief seems.
You understand these roads are not only for trading; the emperor's eyes travel with his own merchants.
Two chiefs argue about a border in words you were never meant to understand.
You remember every word without moving your face; a trader's memory cannot be stolen.
Word travels ahead of you sometimes, of merchants who left the city and were never seen again.
You are wealthy enough to dress like a noble every day, yet you still choose the plainest cloak.
You do not parade your success through the streets, you hold a quiet feast behind closed doors instead.
